questions.question: How many total bones comprise the fully developed adult human skeleton? (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: An adult human skeleton consists of exactly 206 bones, divided into the axial skeleton (80 bones) and the appendicular skeleton (126 bones).

questions.question: How many bones constitute the axial skeleton in adult humans? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton forms the central axis of the human body and contains 80 bones: skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum, hyoid, and auditory ossicles.

questions.question: The longest, heaviest, and strongest bone in the entire human body is the: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, strongest, and heaviest bone in the human body, supporting the entire weight of the upper body during bipedal standing and walking.

questions.question: Which tough, inelastic fibrous connective tissue structure anchors a skeletal muscle securely to a bone? (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: A tendon is a tough band of dense regular fibrous connective tissue composed of collagen that connects skeletal muscle to bone, transmitting the pull of muscle contraction.

questions.question: A strong, flexible band of fibrous connective tissue that connects one bone to another at a joint is called a: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Ligaments are tough, slightly elastic fibrous bands that connect articulating bones together across joints, stabilizing the joint and preventing abnormal dislocation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic anatomical example of a freely movable ball-and-socket joint? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Ball-and-socket joints (found at the shoulder and hip) feature a rounded ball head articulating within a cup-like depression, permitting rotational movement in all planes.

questions.question: The elbow and knee joints permit movement predominantly in a single plane like a door hinge, and are classified as: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Hinge joints permit motion in one plane (flexion and extension), analogous to the hinge of a door. Classic examples include the elbow, knee, and interphalangeal finger joints.

questions.question: The mature living cells responsible for maintaining the extracellular matrix of cartilage are termed:
questions.explanation: Chondrocytes are the specialized living cells embedded in small fluid-filled cavities called lacunae within the dense collagenous matrix of cartilage.

questions.question: Which type of cartilage is the most abundant in the human body, providing a smooth, glassy articulating surface at the ends of long bones? (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Hyaline cartilage is the most widespread cartilage type in humans. It covers the articular surfaces of movable joints and forms the costal cartilages, nasal septum, trachea, and larynx.

questions.question: The tough, shock-absorbing cartilage with dense bundles of thick collagen fibers found in intervertebral discs and the pubic symphysis is:
questions.explanation: Fibrocartilage has exceptional tensile strength and compressibility due to thick parallel bundles of collagen fibers, making it ideal for cushioning vertebral bodies.

questions.question: The flexible cartilage found in the human external ear flap (pinna) and epiglottis that quickly springs back into shape is:
questions.explanation: Elastic cartilage contains an abundant network of branching elastic fibers, granting high flexibility and resilience to structures like the external ear (pinna) and epiglottis.

questions.question: Microscopically, compact bone tissue is organized into repeating cylindrical structural units called: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Compact bone is organized into cylindrical columns called osteons (Haversian systems), each containing concentric rings of matrix (lamellae) surrounding a central neurovascular canal.

questions.question: What is the primary physiological function of red bone marrow located within the trabeculae of spongy bone?

options.B: Hematopoiesis (production of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets)

questions.explanation: Red bone marrow contains pluripotent hematopoietic stem cells that generate all cellular elements of blood: erythrocytes, leukocytes, and thrombocytes.

questions.question: How many pairs of ribs are present in the thoracic cage of the human body?
questions.explanation: Humans have 12 pairs of ribs (24 total): pairs 1-7 are true ribs (attach directly to sternum), pairs 8-10 are false ribs (attach via cartilage), and pairs 11-12 are floating ribs.

questions.question: Which ribs are classified as floating ribs because their anterior ends do not attach to the sternum or adjacent costal cartilage?
questions.explanation: The 11th and 12th rib pairs are termed floating ribs because they terminate in the lateral abdominal musculature without any anterior connection to the sternum.

questions.question: How many total vertebrae constitute the adult human vertebral column?
questions.explanation: In an adult, fusion reduces 33 juvenile vertebrae to 26 articulated bones: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 1 sacrum (5 fused), and 1 coccyx (4 fused).

questions.question: The bones of the human skull that interlock through jagged, immovable fibrous joints are known as:
questions.explanation: Cranial bones are joined tightly by immovable fibrous joints called sutures, interlocking the skull bones to shield the brain from physical trauma.

questions.question: Which bone forms the breastbone positioned centrally in the anterior chest wall where ribs attach?
questions.explanation: The sternum (breastbone) is a flat bone situated along the anterior thoracic midline, anchoring the true ribs via costal cartilages.

questions.question: The pectoral girdle that supports the upper limbs consists of which two pairs of bones? (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: The human pectoral girdle is made up of two clavicles (collarbones) and two scapulae (shoulder blades), connecting each upper arm to the axial skeleton.

questions.question: Which of the following bones is located on the lateral (thumb) side of the human forearm?
questions.explanation: The forearm contains two parallel long bones: the radius situated laterally on the thumb side, and the ulna situated medially on the little finger side.

questions.question: In the human elbow, what happens when the biceps brachii muscle contracts?

options.A: The forearm extends straight at the elbow joint
options.B: The forearm flexes (bends) upward toward the shoulder

questions.explanation: The biceps brachii functions as a flexor muscle: when it contracts, it pulls on its radial insertion, bending (flexing) the forearm at the elbow joint.

questions.question: Which antagonistic muscle contracts to extend (straighten) the human arm at the elbow joint?
questions.explanation: The triceps brachii acts as an extensor muscle. Situated on the posterior arm, its contraction pulls on the olecranon process of the ulna, straightening the arm.

questions.question: Pairs of skeletal muscles that produce opposite physical movements across a joint are termed:
questions.explanation: Antagonistic muscles work in opposing pairs: when one muscle (agonist/flexor) contracts, the opposing partner (antagonist/extensor) relaxes to permit coordinated movement.

questions.question: A systemic metabolic bone disease characterized by a progressive reduction in bone mass and density, making bones fragile and porous, is: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis is a disorder where bone resorption outpaces bone deposition, leading to microarchitectural deterioration, porous bones, and high susceptibility to fractures.

questions.question: Which hormonal decline in aging postmenopausal women is the most significant factor contributing to osteoporosis?
questions.explanation: Estrogen promotes osteoblast activity and preserves bone density. With the cessation of ovarian function after menopause, dropped estrogen triggers rapid bone mineral loss.

questions.question: Inflammation of one or more joints accompanied by pain, swelling, stiffness, and restricted movement is clinically diagnosed as: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Arthritis is a general term denoting inflammation of joints, presenting with joint swelling, pain, warmth, and stiffness.

questions.question: The autoimmune form of arthritis where the body immune system mistakenly attacks synovial membranes of joints is: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune condition where autoantibodies attack the synovial lining of joints, causing chronic inflammation and joint deformities.

questions.question: The small sesamoid bone commonly known as the kneecap that protects the anterior aspect of the knee joint is the:
questions.explanation: The patella (kneecap) is a triangular sesamoid bone embedded within the quadriceps tendon that shields the anterior knee joint and improves mechanical leverage.

questions.question: The lubricating fluid enclosed within the fibrous capsule of freely movable joints that prevents friction between articular cartilages is:
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid is a viscous egg-white-like fluid secreted by the synovial membrane that lubricates articulating joint surfaces, absorbs mechanical shock, and nourishes chondrocytes.

questions.question: Which of the following bones forms the shinbone on the medial weight-bearing side of the human lower leg?
questions.explanation: The tibia (shinbone) is the larger, medial, primary weight-bearing bone of the lower leg, whereas the lateral fibula serves primarily for muscle attachment.

questions.question: How many wrist bones (carpals) are present in each human hand?
questions.explanation: Each human wrist contains 8 small carpal bones arranged in two transverse rows of four, granting flexibility and dexterity to hand movements.

questions.question: The large hip bone (coxal bone) of the human pelvic girdle is formed by the embryonic fusion of which three bones?
questions.explanation: Each coxal (hip) bone develops from the fusion of three separate bones: the superior flaring ilium, the inferior posterior ischium, and the anterior pubis.

questions.question: Why does cartilage take substantially longer to heal after injury compared to vascular bone tissue?

options.A: Cartilage contains dead cells without genetic material
options.B: Cartilage lacks a direct internal blood supply (avascular)
options.C: Cartilage cells are constantly rejected by antibodies
options.D: Cartilage is completely soluble in synovial fluid

questions.explanation: Cartilage is avascular; nutrients and oxygen must slowly diffuse through the dense matrix from surrounding perichondrium, making repair and healing extremely slow.

questions.question: The microscopic concentric rings of mineralized extracellular bone matrix in an osteon are known as:
questions.explanation: Lamellae are concentric layers of hard, calcified collagen matrix that encircle the central Haversian canal inside an osteon.

questions.question: In the human skull, which bone is the ONLY freely movable articulated bone?
questions.explanation: The mandible (lower jaw) is the only movable bone of the adult skull, articulating with the temporal bones at the temporomandibular joints (TMJ) for chewing and speaking.
